stories.title: Bank of America fined $1.2bn for money‑laundering compliance failures
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department announced a $1.2 billion (£910 million) civil penalty for Bank of America after the bank failed to report over $5 billion in suspicious activity, including $1 billion that posed national‑security and illicit‑finance risks. The shortcomings involved not flagging transactions possibly linked to Chinese money‑laundering networks and trade‑based schemes with a substantial nexus to the U.S. southwest border. The announcement came less than 24 hours before the bank’s scheduled quarterly earnings release.
stories.why: A penalty of this scale can increase regulatory scrutiny and compliance costs for a major global financial institution.

stories.title: India and US move closer to trade deal, says External Affairs Minister
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that negotiations on a bilateral trade agreement between India and the United States are advancing toward a “landing point.” Both sides are working to resolve outstanding issues, and officials are actively seeking solutions. He noted the talks are complex because the US is simultaneously concluding competitive agreements with other economies and highlighted the role of tariffs in the US’s re‑industrialisation agenda.
stories.why: The outcome could change tariffs, market access and trade conditions for businesses in both countries.

stories.title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document, the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: IMF warns of risks from AI boom and debt, but raises forecast for world growth
stories.summary: The international body slightly upgraded its outlook for the world economy, but warned that risks of an AI-related market correction and job losses because of the technology, as well as government debt, remain concerns. That's up from its July forecast for three per cent growth and well below the 3.5 per cent expansion in 2025.
stories.why: Changes in the global growth outlook can influence markets, trade, borrowing conditions and business investment across countries.

stories.title: RBI Governor open to more steps to curb FX speculation
stories.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Reserve Bank of India may take additional measures to curb speculative foreign‑exchange trading and ensure orderly movement in the currency market. He said recent restrictions are intended to support genuine hedging needs rather than impose capital controls.
stories.why: RBI action on currency speculation can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
stories.summary: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip , PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.
